classification.difficultyReason: Uses midpoint vectors and a scalar multiple to establish parallelism and a length ratio.

content.prompt: In triangle $ABC$ to the right, $P$ is the midpoint of $AC$ and $Q$ is the midpoint of $BC$. Let $\overrightarrow{AC}=\underset{\sim}{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{CB}=\underset{\sim}{b}$.

spec.description: Unfilled triangle with horizontal AB and midpoint segment PQ. AP and PC have double ticks; CQ and QB have single ticks. Ordinary source grey strokes are rendered black under house style. Coordinates establish the depicted topology and midpoint relationships, not numerical givens.
spec.mathematics: P=(A+C)/2 and Q=(B+C)/2; AP=PC, CQ=QB and PQ is parallel to AB.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry, labels and equal-length ticks are permanent question content.

answer.worked:
$\overrightarrow{AC}=\underset{\sim}{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{CB}=\underset{\sim}{b}$. Since $P$ and $Q$ are midpoints, $AP=PC$ and $QC=QB$.

$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{AB}&=\overrightarrow{AC}+\overrightarrow{CB}\\\overrightarrow{AB}&=\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Hence explain why $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ is parallel to $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and half its length.

answer.worked:
$$\overrightarrow{PQ}=\frac12(\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b})=\frac12\overrightarrow{AB}.$$

The scalar multiple $\frac12$ shows that the vectors are parallel and that $PQ$ is half the length of $AB$.
